deviations.description: gamma, D00: expression parameters after training
deviations.explanation: v2 weights the triplet term of the loss by gamma (`gamma * triplet + regression`, the correction recorded in `training-corrections.json::molir_gamma_weighting`); 1.6.1 reads `gamma` into `self.gamma` and never uses it (`triplet + regression`). With gamma 1 the two losses are the same, with another value the gradients of the encoders differ from the first step on. The variant sets gamma 0.5 on both sides; measured on 2026-10-23, the test predictions differ by up to 0.019 (drug D00, range 0.30) and 0.012 (D01, range 0.50), correlation 0.9989 and 0.9996.
deviations.name: gamma/D00/params_expression

deviations.description: select: selected genes of the samples of the last drug
deviations.detail: non-numeric arrays differ: 1.6.1='NRAS' v2='FKBP4'; 1.6.1='VPS35' v2='PSMD4'; 1.6.1='ADH5' v2='VPS35'
deviations.explanation: 1.6.1 ranks the variance of the expression columns after arcsinh and standardization, where every column has variance 1 up to float rounding, so the top-k columns are decided by rounding noise; v2 ranks the variance of the arcsinh values before standardizing (documented in `literature_models.rst`). The variant keeps 50 of the 2269 genes; measured on 2026-10-23, the two sides share 2 of their 50 genes (about 1 by chance).
deviations.name: select/selected_genes

deviations.description: ragged: features expression of the samples of the last drug
deviations.explanation: 1.6.1 trains one model per drug and fits the scaler (and the variance selection) inside `train` on the samples of that drug's training pairs. v2 featurizes once, on the distinct samples of all training pairs, and then splits the pairs by drug. With a drug that lacks some of the training samples (the last drug here misses the first six), the scaler of that drug differs from the shared one; the case compares the features of the samples of the last drug; measured on 2026-10-23, the standardized expression differs by up to 2.8.
deviations.name: ragged/features_expression

findings: REAL BUG (v2, not fixed here): a preset-built MOLIR cannot finish a fit. `build_components` adds `prediction_mode: PredictionMode.REGRESSION` to the predictor hyperparameters, `MOLIModel.__init__` calls `save_hyperparameters()`, so the checkpoint written with `save_weights_only=True` stores the enum, and the reload of the best epoch (`utils.torch_io.load_state_dict`, `weights_only=True`) raises `UnpicklingError: Unsupported global: drevalpy.types.enums.prediction_mode.PredictionMode`. The predictor tests construct the predictor without `prediction_mode` and do not see it. The case allow-lists the enum (`prediction_mode_checkpoints`) to compare the training; SuperFELTR is built the same way.

The `MOLIModel` of v2 is the 1.6.1 network: a `state_dict` of one loads into the other with `strict=True`, and eval and train mode (batch statistics, dropout, the `normalize(dim=0)` over the batch) agree at the `forward` class.

1.6.1 draws the triplets from `np.random.default_rng(None)` (unseeded: runs are not reproducible), v2 from the global NumPy stream seeded per fit. The case passes the same explicit seed sequence to both (the `random_seed` argument both functions have), so the training steps compare the algorithm and not the draws. A free-running 1.6.1 fit cannot be reproduced at all.
v2 weights the triplet term by `gamma`; 1.6.1 ignores `gamma` (variant `gamma`, deviation). With gamma 1 (variants `default`, `no_es`) the training agrees at the `train` class.

v2 selects the highest-variance expression genes before standardization, 1.6.1 after it (variant `select`, deviation). With `n_gene_expression_features` at least the gene count both keep all genes in the column order of the list and agree exactly. Scaling and selection use the training rows only on both sides.

v2 fits the scaler and the selection once on the samples of all training pairs; 1.6.1 fits them per drug on that drug's samples (variant `ragged`, deviation). The two agree when every drug has the same training samples, which is the case for the complete response matrix of the other variants.

The v2 preset (commit 174ceea7, B5) carries the three `*_intersection` gene lists of the 1.6.1 defaults (`MOLIR.default_gene_lists`); the case does not override them and the selected columns agree. Mutation and copy number columns pass through unchanged on both sides.
